content.comment_body: If a counter has a value of 5 and you turn off the device, is there a method to retain this count after powering it back on? I am using [product_name] software [version_no]. Hardware is [product_name] with [version_no] and [article_no].

Yes, it is possible. Access the Block Properties by right-clicking on the Counter block and selecting Block Properties. In the lower left corner, enable the Retentivity option by clicking on the checkbox. That's all you need to do. Good luck.

analysis.insight_summary: A user asks about retaining the counter's value after a power cycle using [product_name] software and compatible hardware. This demonstrates the need for persistent runtime data and the importance of retentivity features. Another user confirms that this function exists and explains how to activate it through the software interface, showing that while the option is available, it may not be immediately clear to all users.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the counter value on their device to remain unchanged after a restart and wants an easy way to enable this feature within the software.
